title: Now, what if we go downhill?

props.title: Bringing a barge down with Nell

nodes.title: The barge waits in the full chamber

lines.text: Later that day, at the same lock. A barge floats in the full chamber, heading downhill.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Hello! I'm Nell, I keep this lock.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The skipper has been heaving on the lower gates for 5 minutes. They won't move an inch.

options.label: Open the lower paddles
options.text: Let's open the lower paddles and let the chamber drain into the lower canal.

reply.speaker: nell
reply.text: Hear that rush? The water is running out downstream.
The level drops, and the barge sinks gently with it.

options.feedback: Right. The higher water in the chamber was pressing the lower gates shut. Letting it run down to the lower canal brings both levels together.

options.label: Open both paddles
options.text: Let's open the upper and the lower paddles together, to go faster.

reply.speaker: nell
reply.text: Hmm. Now it pours in at the top as fast as it leaves at the bottom.
The level stops halfway. The lower gates still won't budge.

options.feedback: Half right: the lower paddles let water out, but the upper ones keep refilling the chamber. Only the way down should be open.

options.label: Push harder
options.text: Let's push on the balance beams together. The gates must be stuck.

reply.text: The beams creak. The gates don't move.

options.feedback: Tonnes of water press on the chamber side of the gates. No one can push against that: the levels must be equal first.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: There we are: level with the lower canal.

options.label: Open the lower gates
options.text: Now we open the lower gates and let the barge glide out.

reply.speaker: nell
reply.text: Easy as a garden gate. Off she goes!
The gates swing open, and the barge sails into the lower canal.

options.feedback: Yes: with the same level on both sides, nothing holds the gates shut any more.

options.label: Wait a little longer
options.text: Let's wait a few minutes, just to be sure the water has settled.

reply.speaker: nell
reply.text: We can wait. It's already as level as it gets.

options.feedback: Waiting is harmless, but the gates can open as soon as the levels match.

options.label: Open the upper gates
options.text: Let's open the upper gates. That's how the barge came in.

reply.speaker: nell
reply.text: Not a chance! The upper canal is 3 metres above us now.

options.feedback: Now the upper canal holds the higher water, and it presses the upper gates shut. A pair of gates opens only between equal levels.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: See you on the way back up!

props.title: The lock, with the barge in the full chamber

a11y.description: The same lock, seen in three-quarter view. The barge floats in the full chamber, level with the upper canal; the lower gates are shut, with the lower canal 3 metres below. Each choice in the conversation operates the lock: paddles let water through, gates swing or strain, and the barge rises or sinks with the water.

props.textAlternative:
**Text version of the scene.** The barge floats in the lock chamber, which is full: its water is level with the upper canal, 3 m above the lower canal. Both pairs of gates are shut.

What each choice does to the lock:

- **Open the lower paddles:** water runs from the chamber into the lower canal; the chamber empties and the barge goes down with it.
- **Open both paddles:** water runs in at the top as fast as it leaves at the bottom; the level stops halfway.
- **Push on the gates:** the lower gates strain but stay shut, held by the higher water in the chamber.
- **Open the lower gates,** once the chamber is level with the lower canal: they swing open and the barge sails out.
- **Open the upper gates** at that point: they stay shut, held by the higher water of the upper canal.

events.description: Once the conversation ends, show the closing thought and complete the screen.
